rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination - source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Housing discrimination based on the source of lawful income or source of lawful rent or mortgage payment that a tenant or purchaser uses is prohibited. For example, a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
rules.coverage_text: The sale or rental of all property, including open land, whether for business or residential purposes, with listed exceptions.
rules.exemptions: The rental of a single apartment or flat in a two-family dwelling whose other unit is occupied by the owner as a residence at the time of rental; the rental of a room or rooms by the owner or occupant of a one-family dwelling occupied as his/her residence at the time of rental; preference given to persons of the same religion by a religious organization.
rules.penalty: A complaint may be filed with the Division on Civil Rights for free within 180 days of the alleged violation, or in New Jersey Superior Court within two years of the alleged violation.
rules.quoted_span: This means, for example, that a landlord cannot deny the lawful recipient of a Section 8 HUD voucher the right to rent an apartment based solely on that source of lawful income.
